_about: Breaker atoms (Q6166): how a panel schedule's breaker type codes and their legend meanings read as a breaker type, what a row says when it is a spare or a space, and what each type is bought as. A schedule's legend decides what its own codes mean; the code lists are the fallback for a code the legend does not define. Order matters: the first feature a code matches is its feature (equipment ground fault before personnel ground fault).

words: COMBINATION ARC FAULT AND GROUND FAULT
features.source: UL 1699 / UL 943 combination devices: a dual-function breaker is both an AFCI and a GFCI
NEC 426.28 / 427.22 ground-fault protection of equipment (30 mA class), UL 1053
NEC 210.8 ground-fault circuit-interrupter protection for personnel, UL 943
a shunt-trip breaker (remote trip coil), as the schedule marks it
NEC 440.22 / UL 489 HACR-rated breaker for heating, air-conditioning and refrigeration equipment

by_circuit._about: A breaker row whose codes name no protection (Q6350): its type decided per circuit by what the circuit serves, never one type for a whole panel. Arc fault where the circuit is a dwelling unit's or a guest room's 120 V single-pole 15/20 A one (a typical unit's rooms, rooms named as one: unit_name_words; a room's own panel's room or every device on the circuit in one); ground fault at the breaker for a load the code puts on a GFCI unless a GFCI device on the circuit carries it (a GFCI receptacle, or the one coderules.json E-RECEPT-GFCI makes the circuit's GFCI): then the breaker has none; both make a dual-function breaker, neither a standard one. A schedule that marks types on other rows prints this one standard: the build installs what the code wants and keeps the printed type as its design.

arc_fault.rule: every 120 V single-phase 15 and 20 A branch circuit supplying outlets or devices in a dwelling unit, or in a hotel or motel guest room or guest suite, is AFCI protected

by_circuit.unit_name_source: a room is a dwelling unit's or a guest room's when it is a typical unit's room (the spec's unit instances) or its name has one of these phrases (a guest laundry or a guest corridor is neither)
by_circuit.device_rule: a GFCI receptacle on the circuit carries its ground-fault protection (coderules.json E-RECEPT-GFCI; the alternative, a GFCI breaker and standard receptacles)
by_circuit.volts_unread: the schedule prints no voltage: a single-pole branch breaker taken as 120 V (a dwelling or guest unit's panel is 120/240 or 208Y/120 V)
by_circuit.nothing_needed: no code rule wants AFCI or GFCI protection at this circuit's breaker

default_source: a schedule row whose codes (and their legend) name no protection: a standard thermal-magnetic breaker
pole_step_source: panelboard circuit numbering: odd numbers on the left bus side, even on the right, so a multi-pole breaker numbered n also takes n+2 (and n+4)
panel_rule: a panel is one the documents establish: its panel schedule, the one-line or the riser (a feeder to or from it), or gear the documents place; a circuit label naming any other panel is a finding for review, never a new panel
unknown_panel_reason: the circuit label names no panel of the documents: it is no panel's circuit until they settle it (a misread mark beside the device, or a panel the documents leave out)
